item.title: Dangote accepts Bae U Barbie’s invitation to appear on YouTube show
item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, has agreed to appear on Nigerian content creator Bae U Barbie’s YouTube programme, Curiosity Made Me Ask, following an invitation to engage younger audiences. Bae U Barbie, born Adebayo Ridwan, extended the invitation while questioning the billionaire about his media engagements and the need to reach young Nigerians interested in his business and its planned initial public offering (IPO). The content creator observed that most of Dangote’s interviews had been conducted on platforms that were not popular among younger audiences, despite their interest in investing in his company. “Most of the interviews we’ve seen you have been on platforms that my generation don’t watch,” Bae U Barbie said. He clarified that he was not asking Dangote to dismiss his media team but urged the businessman to consider appearing on his show after completing his existing engagements. “I’m not saying you should sack your media team. No, but you know, when you finish,” he said before asking when the billionaire would feature on the programme. Responding, Dangote acknowledged the importance of engaging younger Nigerians, describing them as the country’s future while admitting that his generation had not done enough for Nigeria and Africa. “Honestly, the future that we have is actually you, the youth. We, our own generation, really, we have not really done very well for Nigeria and also for Africa. That’s the truth,” he said. The billionaire stressed the need for older Nigerians to share their experiences with younger people to help them understand the country’s history and development. “So we need to sit down with some of you and discuss our own experience with you,” he added. Dangote also observed that many young Nigerians were unfamiliar with some prominent figures and events from the country’s past. He cited former President Olusegun Obasanjo, suggesting that younger people might know more about him because he returned to power. Bae U Barbie interrupted to highlight his own contribution to making Obasanjo accessible to younger audiences, saying, “Thanks to me. item.title: Troops rescue 11 passengers, foil kidnap attempt in Kogi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 12 Composite Brigade of the Nigerian Army have foiled a kidnapping attempt and rescued 11 passengers along Kabba-Ayere Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the incident occurred on October 18, 2026. He said troops deployed at the patrol base in Kabba were on routine patrol when they responded to credible intelligence about suspected terrorists attempting to abduct passengers travelling in a commercial vehicle along the route. “On arrival, the troops made contact with the terrorists and engaged them, forcing them to abandon the victims and flee into the surrounding bush,” he said. Abdullahi said nine passengers, including the driver, were rescued during the initial operation. He added that the driver and two other passengers who sustained injuries were evacuated for medical attention, while the commercial vehicle was handed over to the appropriate authorities. According to him, troops conducted a follow-up operation on October 19, 2026, during which they searched the area and rescued two additional passengers who had fled into the bush during the encounter. The operation brought the total number of rescued passengers to 11. Abdullahi said the operation underscored the brigade’s commitment to protecting lives and property, denying terrorists freedom of action and improving the safety of commuters across Kogi State. He urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. The Nigerian Army, he added, remained committed to sustaining efforts to safeguard lives and property and ensure the security of residents of Kogi State. item.title: ‘It’s easier you put me in prison than take my phone away’ — Dangote
item.description: Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote has said he would rather be imprisoned than have his phone taken away, describing losing access to the device as a “no-go area”. Dangote made the remark at an event in Lagos where he unveiled his “Vision 2030” plan for Africa’s industrial revolution. During the event, the billionaire businessman was asked to choose between spending one week without his phone or giving up access to his private jet. Responding to the question, Dangote said he would find it more difficult to part with his phone than his private jet. “Ah… I think it’s easier you put me in prison than to take my phone away. So, you know, I mean taking my phone away is no-go area, okay?” The industrialist also revealed that he has more than 13,000 contacts saved on his phone, highlighting the importance of the device in maintaining his extensive network of personal and professional relationships. “I know that would be almost… my number — I have that number since… Twitter… I have more than 13,000 contacts on my phone.” Reacting to the size of his contact list, Dangote added that he rarely blocks people, suggesting that this has contributed to the large number of contacts on his device. “Wow. Wow. I hardly… I don’t like blocking people, so a lot of people” His comments offer a glimpse into how the billionaire uses his phone to maintain connections, even as he oversees business interests spanning manufacturing, cement, fertiliser, oil refining and other sectors across Africa. Dangote is the president and chief executive of Dangote Group, one of Africa’s largest industrial conglomerates. item.title: Otti signs laws toughening penalties for cultism, rape, kidnapping
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, on Monday signed four laws strengthening legal provisions against cultism, rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, child exploitation and vandalism of public infrastructure. The new legislation also provides for a sex offenders’ register, addresses offences involving electronic records and digital assets, and introduces restorative justice mechanisms to make offenders accountable for harm caused by their actions. Otti assented to the four bills passed by the eighth Abia State House of Assembly at a ceremony held at the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia. The laws are the Abia State Criminal Law No. 7 of 2026, the Administration of Criminal Justice Law No. 6 of 2026, the Restorative Justice Law No. 8 of 2026 and the Abia State University Amendment No. 2 Law No. 4 of 2026. Explaining the crime-fighting provisions, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Mr Ikechukwu Uwanna, said the new Criminal Law strengthened measures against unlawful societies and secret cults by addressing membership, sponsorship, meetings and the management of such groups. He said the provisions extended beyond educational institutions to communities, widening the scope of the state’s response to cult-related activities. The law also provides sanctions for vandalising government infrastructure and dealing in stolen public assets, while strengthening legal protections against rape, sexual assault, sexual harassment and spousal violence. Uwanna said the legislation recognised both male and female rape victims and provided for a sex offenders’ register to promote accountability. Other provisions target kidnapping, child exploitation, corporate responsibility and offences involving electronic records and digital assets. The Attorney-General said the reforms were informed by public concerns over cult violence, kidnapping, the destruction of public facilities, sexual violence and delays in criminal proceedings. Otti vows strict enforcement Speaking during the signing ceremony, Otti said his administration was determined to ensure strict compliance with the new laws, noting that gaps in existing legislation had sometimes constrained the enforcement of government policies. item.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day suspension after Portugal camp walkout
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension for leaving the Portuguese national team camp during the UEFA Nations League, the country’s football federation (FPF) announced on Monday. The 41-year-old left the Portugal camp on September 30, before accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. item.title: Aviation unions petition NSA over alleged Air Peace runway invasion
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Some aviation unions have petitioned the National Security Adviser, NSA, demanding an investigation into an alleged runway and taxiway invasion involving the country’s largest carrier, Air Peace, during the picketing of the airline on August 11, 2026. Meanwhile, a source close to the airline told Vanguard that it did not invade the runway or taxiway. The source said: “No, it did not happen. Also, there is no reaction from us yet.” However, the unions, Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, ATSSSAN, National Association of Aircraft Pilots and Engineers, NAAPE, and National Union of Air Transport Employees, NUATE, urged the NSA to initiate a discreet forensic investigation into the incident and ensure that everyone found responsible, including those who authorised the deployment of buses, was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the Terrorism Act and the Civil Aviation Act. They also called on the NSA to direct the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to preserve and release all closed-circuit television footage, air traffic control voice recordings and airside vehicle logs relating to the incident. item.content:encoded: By Dickson Omobola Some aviation unions have petitioned the National Security Adviser, NSA, demanding an investigation into an alleged runway and taxiway invasion involving the country’s largest carrier, Air Peace, during the picketing of the airline on August 11, 2026. Meanwhile, a source close to the airline told Vanguard that it did not invade the runway or taxiway. The source said: “No, it did not happen. Also, there is no reaction from us yet.” However, the unions, Air Transport Services Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, ATSSSAN, National Association of Aircraft Pilots and Engineers, NAAPE, and National Union of Air Transport Employees, NUATE, urged the NSA to initiate a discreet forensic investigation into the incident and ensure that everyone found responsible, including those who authorised the deployment of buses, was arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the Terrorism Act and the Civil Aviation Act. They also called on the NSA to direct the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, to preserve and release all closed-circuit television footage, air traffic control voice recordings and airside vehicle logs relating to the incident. General Secretary of ATSSSAN, Frances Akinjole; Deputy General Secretary of NAAPE, Umoh Ofonime; and General Secretary of NUATE, Paul Igene, copied the petition to the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, DSS, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, and the Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA. The petition reads: “We, the above-named aviation trade unions, respectfully bring to your esteemed office a grave and unprecedented breach of national aviation security that occurred on August 11, 2026, at the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. “The joint unions issued the required lawful notices of picketing against 16 domestic airlines, most of which are members of the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON, operating in Nigeria for two grievous infractions: “Flagrant refusal and obstruction of the unionisation of their employees, in direct violation of Section 40 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), Section 9 of the Labour Act, the Trade Unions Act, and ILO Conventions 87 and 98, ratified by Nigeria. “Wilful and persistent refusal to remit the Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) already collected from passengers. The TSC is a statutory charge meant to be shared among aviation agencies (NCAA, NAMA, NiMet, NSIB and NCAT) for safety oversight, training and the proper functioning of the sector. “A more debilitating assault on the psyche of agency workers, who are our union members, is that the non-remittance of the TSC has rendered the implementation of the various duly negotiated collective bargaining agreements of the agencies nugatory, and agitated staff were becoming uncontrollable. This was seen as an accident waiting to happen. “To avoid a total shutdown of Nigerian airspace at once and in the interest of the travelling public, the joint unions strategically resolved to picket the defaulting airlines sequentially, one after the other, each day. Air Peace Airlines was scheduled for August 11, 2026. “The picketing was peaceful, lawful and conducted at the airline’s operational office/counter area, not on the airside. During the barricades, staff of Air Peace also became physically violent against unarmed union members performing their lawful trade union duties. They incited passengers against the union members, but the unions conducted themselves decorously, remaining unprovoked and undeterred. “The action was, however, suspended on the afternoon of the first day following the welcome intervention of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the security agencies at the airport. “In reaction to the lawful picketing, Air Peace Airlines became frustrated that other defaulting airlines were allowed to operate that day. In a reckless and dangerous act of self-help and sabotage, the management and staff of Air Peace Airlines mobilised five of its branded buses and deliberately drove them onto and parked them across the taxiway and manoeuvring area of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, with the clear intent to block all aircraft movement, prevent other airlines from operating and possibly cause an accident. “This incursion shut down all flight operations from Lagos for hours, endangered the lives of passengers, crew and airport workers, exposed the airport to the risk of a catastrophic aircraft collision, and violated sterile airside security protocols. “This act transcends a labour dispute. It constitutes an act of terrorism under Section 2(3)(d) and (f) of the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022, involving the wilful obstruction, sabotage and interference with critical national infrastructure and aviation facilities. “It is also a violation of the Civil Aviation Act, 2022, Part XIX, involving unlawful interference with aviation, trespass on the manoeuvring area and endangerment of aircraft. “It poses a threat to International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) safety and security standards, to which Nigeria is a signatory, bringing Nigeria into international ridicule and exposing the country to a potential Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) category downgrade. “If left unchecked, this dangerous precedent would empower any aggrieved airline to seize a runway and hold the entire nation to ransom. In the interest of national integrity, aviation safety and sovereignty, we most respectfully pray the National Security Adviser to: “Immediately cause a discreet and thorough forensic investigation into the runway/taxiway invasion of August 11, 2026, by a joint security team led by your office and involving the DSS, NCAA AVSEC and FAAN AVSEC. Identify, arrest and prosecute all persons found culpable, including those who authorised the deployment of the five buses, in accordance with the Terrorism Act and the Civil Aviation Act. “Direct FAAN to preserve and release all CCTV footage, ATC voice recordings and airside vehicle logs from that day. “Direct the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to impose severe sanctions on Air Peace Airlines for bringing the aviation sector into ridicule and endangering public safety. “Compel the relevant regulatory authorities to enforce compliance with the remittance of the Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) and strict adherence to labour laws guaranteeing the right to unionisation across all domestic airlines. “Ensure the protection of union members and aviation agency staff who are now targets of intimidation for performing their lawful duties. We have absolute confidence in your office as the custodian of national security and assure you of our cooperation. However, it is our utmost expectation that this matter will be given the prompt attention it deserves without delay.” The post Aviation unions petition NSA over alleged Air Peace runway invasion appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC campaign knocks Oyedele over ₦4,000/$ fuel subsidy warning
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Director of Media and Publicity of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, has challenged the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, to publish the economic model behind his warning that a return to fuel subsidy could push the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar. Ologbondiyan accused the Federal Government of using fear to discourage debate on fuel subsidy, insisting that Nigerians deserve evidence, not alarming projections, on the potential economic consequences of restoring the policy. Speaking to Vanguard, he described the minister’s warning as scaremongering and demanded that the government explain how it arrived at the projected exchange rate. “The Minister of Finance is merely scaremongering. He cannot claim that a return to fuel subsidy will cause the naira to depreciate to ₦4,000 to the dollar without showing Nigerians the model behind that projection,” he said. Ologbondiyan questioned the reliance on investors’ concerns to oppose a subsidy return, challenging the government to identify those behind the projections and disclose their calculations. “They should show Nigerians who is making these claims and explain how they arrived at an exchange rate of ₦4,000 to the dollar if fuel subsidy is reintroduced,” he said. He also argued that Nigeria was not the only country to consider or operate a production subsidy, maintaining that the proposal should be assessed on its economic merits rather than dismissed through dire forecasts. “I do not believe this projection is realistic. It is fantasy,” he said. Oyedele had warned that a return to fuel subsidy could send the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar, while also raising concerns about investors’ perception of the opposition. Ologbondiyan questioned the reliance on investors’ concerns to oppose a subsidy return, challenging the government to identify those behind the projections and disclose their calculations. “They should show Nigerians who is making these claims and explain how they arrived at an exchange rate of ₦4,000 to the dollar if fuel subsidy is reintroduced,” he said. He also argued that Nigeria was not the only country to consider or operate a production subsidy, maintaining that the proposal should be assessed on its economic merits rather than dismissed through dire forecasts. “I do not believe this projection is realistic. It is fantasy,” he said. Oyedele had warned that a return to fuel subsidy could send the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar, while also raising concerns about investors’ perception of the opposition. Vice-President Kashim Shettima unveiled the Nigerian Capital Market Master Plan 2.0 at the National Capital Market Conference 2026 in Abuja on Monday, describing the market as a critical platform for mobilising long-term financing for infrastructure and economic development. The plan, developed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), targets growth from a baseline of about ₦250 trillion to ₦750 trillion over the next decade. Shettima said Nigeria’s capital market had recorded significant growth since President Bola Tinubu assumed office in May 2023. According to him, the Nigerian Exchange All-Share Index rose from about 55,000 points in May 2023 to more than 260,000 points, while the value of listed equities increased from approximately ₦30 trillion to nearly ₦160 trillion in January 2026. He added that the combined value of the equity and bond markets had exceeded ₦217 trillion, reflecting increased investor participation and the impact of economic reforms. The Vice-President attributed the growth to Federal Government reforms, including the removal of petrol subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange market, tax reforms, bank recapitalisation and the enactment of the Investments and Securities Act 2025. He said the master plan would place the capital market at the centre of infrastructure financing, enabling governments and businesses to raise long-term funds locally rather than rely excessively on short-term or foreign borrowing. Shettima added that the plan would strengthen the bond market for state and subnational governments, broaden retail participation through technology and investor education, and enable businesses in agriculture, solid minerals and other sectors to raise capital locally. The Vice-President, who chairs the National Economic Council, said he would work with state governors to encourage responsible capital market financing through properly structured bonds, credible project pipelines and greater transparency. He said such financing could promote fiscal discipline and strengthen accountability in public spending, warning that policy reversals could undermine investor confidence and erode recent gains. However, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister for the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said Nigeria should target a $1 trillion capital market within the next decade to support its ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030. Oyedele urged the government to accelerate the listing of selected state-owned enterprises, particularly NNPC and NLNG, arguing that making their shares available to investors would deepen the market, improve transparency and broaden public ownership of national assets. He said the government would also introduce incentives to encourage privately owned Nigerian companies to list on the Nigerian Exchange rather than compel them to do so. “We cannot force them. We would encourage Nigerian private businesses to list. We will use incentives to attract them,” he said. Oyedele argued that listing NNPC and NLNG could significantly expand Nigeria’s capital market, drawing a comparison with Saudi Aramco, the Saudi Arabian oil company. He said the initiative would enable Nigerians to participate in the wealth generated by national assets while creating more investment opportunities for domestic and international investors. Under the proposed master plan, the government is targeting an increase in equity market capitalisation from 33 per cent of gross domestic product to at least 60 per cent, while raising the number of listed companies from 146 to 250 and expanding the retail investor base from six million to 20 million. Other targets include more than tripling corporate bond issuance as a share of GDP, increasing sukuk market penetration from 0.3 per cent to at least five per cent of GDP, and raising pension assets from six per cent to 16 per cent of GDP. Oyedele said Nigeria was also working to improve its standing among international investors, citing the country’s reinstatement in the FTSE Russell Frontier Market Index on September 21, 2026, and the inclusion of Nigerian government bonds in a new J.P. Morgan government bond index, with a weight of 7.4 per cent. He said the government was seeking a return to J.P. Morgan’s flagship government bond index and an eventual upgrade to emerging-market status. The minister added that the government was targeting an investment-grade credit rating within three years, noting that this would require sustained reforms, improved market liquidity and reliable repatriation of foreign investors’ funds. As part of efforts to deepen domestic investment, Oyedele formally launched the National Savings Scheme, designed to provide Nigerians with regulated avenues to save and invest towards education, housing, business development and retirement. He said the scheme would offer accessible investment channels, transparent information, reasonable costs and a functional complaints process, with tax incentives provided within the law. Oyedele expressed concern that many young Nigerians were investing their money in betting platforms, unregulated cryptocurrency schemes and Ponzi schemes instead of regulated investment products. He said the scheme would help channel domestic savings into productive investments, including through small contributions made using mobile phones. The minister also announced plans to strengthen enforcement against Ponzi schemes through improved surveillance, social media monitoring and collaboration with law enforcement agencies. He added that the government was considering a fraud restitution mechanism to support victims. Speaking at the conference, SEC Director-General Dr Emomotimi Agama said the master plan was designed to deepen market participation, expand investment products and strengthen the integrity and infrastructure of the capital market. He disclosed that a Project Steering Committee and a Capital Market Master Plan Implementation Committee would be inaugurated to oversee implementation. “Every commitment in NCMMP 2.0 will have an owner, a timeline and a scorecard, and we will report progress openly to this nation,” he said. Agama said equity market capitalisation crossed ₦100 trillion for the first time in January and rose above ₦160 trillion in September, while the All-Share Index gained about 60 per cent in 2026, following a 51 per cent return in 2025. However, he warned that the increase in market value had not been matched by sufficient participation among Nigerians, noting that too few citizens owned shares, bonds or units in collective investment schemes. “The strength of any capital market rests on the savings of its people. Ours must rest on the savings of all of us,” he said. The post FG targets ₦750tn capital market, seeks NNPC, NLNG listing appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France announces partial curfew, ban on protests in Paris
item.description: France imposed a partial curfew and banned demonstrations in parts of Paris on Monday, police said, as the government sought to restore order after some of the worst street violence in years. The Paris police prefecture said the partial curfew would be in effect from 11:00 pm (2100 GMT) on Monday until 6:00 am on Tuesday in several neighbourhoods of the French capital. Demonstrations were also banned in several Paris neighbourhoods from 8:00 pm on Monday until 6:00 am on Tuesday. item.title: Katsina police arrest six suspects, recover 2,970 drug items
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina The Katsina State Police Command has arrested six suspected illicit drug dealers in separate operations across the state, recovering 2,970 items, including suspected illicit drugs and substances believed to be Indian hemp. The command said the recoveries included Pregabalin, Exol, Tramadol and a substance suspected to be methamphetamine, commonly known as ICE. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, disclosed this in a statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Ali Umar Fage, on October 19, 2026. According to the statement, the operations involved police operatives, members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (JTF) and local vigilantes. The first operation occurred on October 9, when members of the Civilian JTF in Bakori Local Government Area arrested a 23-year-old suspect, Abdullahi Muntari, at about 2 p.m. over alleged involvement in illicit drug trafficking. The police said 41 pieces of a substance suspected to be ICE were recovered from the suspect. Muntari allegedly confessed to receiving supplies from his elder brother, Adamu Muntari, who is currently at large, and distributing the substance in Kakumi village and neighbouring communities. The command further alleged that the suspect supplied illicit drugs to armed bandits operating in Bakori and its environs. In a separate operation on October 13, at about 11:30 p.m., vigilantes in Kartaka village, Charanci Local Government Area, intercepted a red motorcycle conveying three suspects following intelligence reports. The suspects were identified as Babangida Mamman, Basiru Isah and Saminu Sada. According to the statement, the suspects allegedly failed to stop when flagged down, leading to a pursuit during which they sustained varying degrees of injuries while attempting to evade arrest. They were subsequently taken to a nearby hospital for medical attention. A search reportedly led to the recovery of 2,000 Pregabalin tablets, 765 Exol tablets and 29 Tramadol capsules, bringing the total to 2,794 items. item.title: Six soldiers, major feared dead in Yobe ambush
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri At least six soldiers, including a major, and scores of suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists are feared dead following an ambush on a military convoy near Kanamma village in Geidam Local Government Area of Yobe State. Sources said the attack occurred at about 4 p.m. on Monday, when the convoy, led by a commanding officer, came under attack. According to a report by local online publication Yerwa Express News, the attackers targeted the military convoy near Kanamma. A source said the lead vehicle was hit by an explosive device before the attackers opened fire on other vehicles in the convoy. “The commanding officer and three other soldiers in the first vehicle died in the initial attack, while three additional soldiers were killed with scores of the attackers during the ensuing exchange of gunfire,” the source said. The identities of the officers and soldiers were not immediately available, while the number of casualties among the attackers could not be independently verified as of press time. Sources, however, said troops inflicted heavy losses on the attackers during the exchange of gunfire. The ambush comes amid persistent security challenges along the Geidam-Kanamma and Mayamti routes, which sources said had remained closed for months because of terrorist activities. Army Arrests Suspected Terrorist Collaborator In a related development, troops of the Nigerian Army’s 27 Task Force Brigade have arrested a suspected terrorist collaborator in Kanamma town, Geidam Local Government Area. Security sources told our correspondent that the suspect was arrested at about 12:15 p.m. on October 17 during security operations in the area. Preliminary investigations reportedly indicated that the suspect was on a wanted list in connection with alleged terrorist activities within the brigade’s area of responsibility. The sources said troops had intensified operations to dismantle terrorist networks across the North-East. The latest developments come hours after the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, visited the Theatre Command Headquarters of the Joint Task Force, North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, in an engagement aimed at boosting troops’ morale. item.title: Two suffer severe burns as tanker falls from Otedola bridge
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Two people sustained severe burn injuries on Monday when a 33,000-litre diesel-laden tanker plunged from Otedola Bridge and burst into flames beneath the bridge along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The incident, which occurred at about 3pm, caused panic among motorists and passers-by as the tanker reportedly fell from the bridge while conveying petroleum products from a depot. Eyewitnesses said motorists hurriedly diverted while pedestrians fled in different directions to escape the inferno. Emergency responders rescued the two victims from the danger zone and evacuated them for urgent medical attention. Men of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service from the Alausa and Ikeja fire stations were mobilised to the scene to contain the fire. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), working with other emergency management agencies, also participated in the rescue operation. The injured victims were subsequently evacuated by the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency’s Rescue Unit to the Lagos State Accident and Emergency Centre, Toll-Gate, where they were admitted for treatment. Other agencies involved in the coordinated rescue and containment operations included the Federal Road Safety Corps, Lagos State Neighbourhood Safety Agency and police personnel from the Alausa Police Division. Commending the response of the agencies, LASTMA General Manager, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, praised the emergency responders for their efforts in rescuing and evacuating the victims while supporting operations to contain the fire. He reiterated LASTMA’s commitment to traffic regulation enforcement, efficient traffic management, prompt incident response and coordination of emergency operations across Lagos State. Bakare-Oki urged motorists, particularly operators of heavy-duty and articulated vehicles, to conduct regular mechanical inspections, comply with prescribed safety standards and adopt responsible driving practices to prevent avoidable road accidents. Meanwhile, damping-down operations were still ongoing as of 5pm to eliminate residual hotspots and prevent the fire from reigniting. The immediate and remote causes of the incident had yet to be established as of press time. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Mrs Margaret Adeseye, reaffirmed the service’s commitment to protecting lives and property through prompt and effective emergency response. She also urged motorists to exercise caution around emergency scenes and comply with safety instructions issued by emergency responders. item.title: Grid supply crashes 81% to 675MW as nine plants go offline
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s grid electricity supply plunged by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW at noon, following a reduction in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 12. The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to alert customers to supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW. However, by 1pm, the number of plants supplying the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply fell to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour. Among the plants reported to have gone offline were Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants. The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before plunging to 675MW at 1pm. Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, an increase of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak. In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge. The company said TCN’s technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that supply was gradually being restored to its feeders. “We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits,” AEDC said, apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption. Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of electricity allocated to it from the national grid. In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply. It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible. item.title: Video: NAFDAC uncovers suspected counterfeit whisky factory in Aba
item.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) says it has uncovered a suspected counterfeit alcoholic drinks factory in Aba, Abia State, with equipment and materials recovered from the facility estimated to be worth more than ₦500 million. The agency said the facility, located at No. 25 Omenazu Street, was discovered following credible intelligence about suspected illegal production activities. In a statement posted on X on Monday, NAFDAC said its officials found the facility operating under unhygienic conditions. It added that the suspected operator fled when the enforcement team arrived, abandoning a vehicle containing materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and Scottish Hills Whisky. NAFDAC has uncovered a suspected counterfeit alcoholic drinks factory at Aba, Abia State, following a tip off. The operator reportedly fled when officials arrived, leaving behind a vehicle containing fake packaging materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and… pic.twitter.com/R5zoHy3fK4 — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) October 19, 2026 “Counterfeit packaging materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and Scottish Hills Whisky, empty bottles and a drum containing approximately 200 litres of liquid were found” in the vehicle, the agency said. NAFDAC said further searches inside the facility led to the discovery of materials and equipment allegedly used in the production and packaging of the suspected counterfeit drinks. According to the agency, the items included bottle caps, sealing machines, empty bottles, cartons, packaging materials and tanks containing different liquid concoctions. Officials also found dirty sieves reportedly used in the production process, as well as plastic buckets and 200-litre drums containing ethanol. “Drums containing ethanol and tree bark immersed in ethanol were also discovered,” NAFDAC said, adding that the findings raised serious concerns about the safety and quality of the products allegedly being manufactured at the facility. The agency put the estimated value of the equipment, materials and other components recovered from the facility at more than ₦500 million. NAFDAC urged members of the public to assist its enforcement efforts by providing credible information about suspected illegal manufacturing operations. “The Agency urges members of the public to provide credible information on suspected illegal manufacturing activities to the NAFDAC,” the statement said. In a statement posted on X on Monday, NAFDAC said its officials found the facility operating under unhygienic conditions. It added that the suspected operator fled when the enforcement team arrived, abandoning a vehicle containing materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and Scottish Hills Whisky. NAFDAC has uncovered a suspected counterfeit alcoholic drinks factory at Aba, Abia State, following a tip off. The operator reportedly fled when officials arrived, leaving behind a vehicle containing fake packaging materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and… pic.twitter.com/R5zoHy3fK4 — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) October 19, 2026 “Counterfeit packaging materials bearing the names of Sir Edwards Scotch Whisky and Scottish Hills Whisky, empty bottles and a drum containing approximately 200 litres of liquid were found” in the vehicle, the agency said. NAFDAC said further searches inside the facility led to the discovery of materials and equipment allegedly used in the production and packaging of the suspected counterfeit drinks. According to the agency, the items included bottle caps, sealing machines, empty bottles, cartons, packaging materials and tanks containing different liquid concoctions. Officials also found dirty sieves reportedly used in the production process, as well as plastic buckets and 200-litre drums containing ethanol. “Drums containing ethanol and tree bark immersed in ethanol were also discovered,” NAFDAC said, adding that the findings raised serious concerns about the safety and quality of the products allegedly being manufactured at the facility. The agency put the estimated value of the equipment, materials and other components recovered from the facility at more than ₦500 million. NAFDAC urged members of the public to assist its enforcement efforts by providing credible information about suspected illegal manufacturing operations. “The Agency urges members of the public to provide credible information on suspected illegal manufacturing activities to the NAFDAC,” the statement said. item.title: VIDEO: Two Injured As Tanker Plunges From Otedola Bridge, Bursts Into Flames
item.description: Two people were severely injured after a diesel tanker plunged off the Otedola Bridge — along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Lagos — and erupted into a “ferocious inferno beneath the bridge”. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said the “terrifying conflagration left two victims with extensive and severe burn injuries, necessitating their immediate extrication from the danger zone and urgent medical intervention”. LASTMA’s Director, Public Affairs and Enlightenment Department, Adebayo Taofiq, however, said the agency’s emergency response team, in concert with other relevant emergency management agencies, “swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued the two severely burnt victims from the perilous situation.” “The injured victims were subsequently evacuated by the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency’s Rescue Unit (LRU) to the Lagos State Accident and Emergency Centre, Toll Gate, where they were admitted for immediate medical attention,” Taofiq said in a statement on Monday evening.
